title: The Races With the Longest Track Record
meta_description: A 40th edition, a 33rd edition, a 31st edition -- some of Southeast Asia's races have been run for decades. Edition count is a real, underrated signal of organizational experience.
dek: A race that's survived 20, 30, or 40 editions has, by definition, solved the logistics problems that cause many newer events to falter in their first few years. These are the region's clearest examples of decades-deep staying power.

sections.heading: Chombueng Marathon: 40 Editions and Counting
paragraphs: The Chombueng Marathon, held at Ratchaburi Rajabhat University in Thailand, is now in its 40th edition -- a genuinely long track record relative to most of the region's races, and a strong signal that its organizers have had decades to refine everything from aid-station placement to course marking.
A university-hosted race running this long also suggests a stable, ongoing institutional relationship behind it, rather than a one-off event that happened to be hosted on a campus once.

sections.heading: Amazing Thailand Pattaya Marathon: 33 Editions
paragraphs: The Amazing Thailand Pattaya Marathon, in its 33rd edition, brings the same kind of accumulated experience to one of Thailand's best-established tourist destinations -- a race that's had over three decades to work out exactly the details that matter most to both local and international entrants.

Pattaya's long-established tourist infrastructure alongside this race's own history makes it a particularly low-friction pick for a first-time visitor who wants a well-worn, predictable event rather than a newer one still finding its footing.

sections.heading: Thai Sikh Run and Khon Kaen International Marathon: Deep Community and Regional Roots
paragraphs: The Thai Sikh Run, in its 31st edition, and the Khon Kaen International Marathon, in its 22nd edition, both represent decades of continuous running in their respective communities -- the former rooted in Bangkok's Sikh community, the latter serving northeastern Thailand's Isaan region. Both are strong picks for a runner who's already covered the country's biggest tourist-city races and wants an event with its own deep, specific local history.

Long-running community and regional races like these tend to carry a genuinely different atmosphere from a newer, more internationally marketed event -- often smaller, more locally attended, and shaped by decades of the same community showing up year after year.

sections.heading: Sihanoukville International Half Marathon: Cambodia's Established Entry
paragraphs: The Sihanoukville International Half Marathon, in its 12th edition, gives Cambodia its own genuinely established race with real staying power -- worth knowing about specifically since Cambodia's overall race count is much smaller than its neighbors', and a 12-edition track record in that context is a meaningful signal of stability.
For a runner building a race circuit across less-covered parts of the region, an event with this kind of continuity is a safer bet than a newer, unproven race in the same country.

faqs.question: What's the longest-running race in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Among the races in this site's own data, the Chombueng Marathon at Ratchaburi Rajabhat University in Thailand has the longest track record at 40 editions, followed by the Amazing Thailand Pattaya Marathon at 33 editions and the Thai Sikh Run at 31 editions.

faqs.question: Why does a race's edition count matter when choosing where to race?
faqs.answer: A race that's survived 20, 30, or 40 editions has, by definition, solved the logistics problems -- aid-station placement, course marking, cutoff timing -- that cause many newer events to falter in their first few years. It's a genuine, underrated signal of organizational experience.

faqs.question: Does Cambodia have an established, long-running race?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the Sihanoukville International Half Marathon is in its 12th edition, a meaningful track record given Cambodia's overall race count is much smaller than its neighbors', making it a comparatively safe, established pick for that country.

editorial_notes: Editorial picks based on this site's own researched race-entity data (see this site's country round-up articles and regions/races index for full listings) -- not a third-party or sponsored ranking.
